subject: Least-privilege audit & provisioning evidence request — Aurora Inc
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@aurora-inc.com>
To: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aurora Procurement <procure@aurora-inc.com>
Date: 2027-04-11 09:12 -0700
Subject: Request: least-privilege matrix + provisioning proof for SIG review

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Aurora is moving through the SIG review and the security team has a couple of focused asks before we can clear you for pilot access. Could you provide: 

- A least-privilege access matrix showing roles, permissions, and example scoped policies (read/write/admin) for the Redwood Console and Dedicated endpoints.
- Evidence of SSO/SAML configuration (IdP metadata, ACS URL) and SCIM provisioning attributes mapping.
- A short sample of audit logs showing user provisioning events (just filenames/timestamps are fine) — sanitized.

If possible please send the artifacts by EOD Tuesday (Aurora time). We may follow up with a quick call to walk through the matrix.

Thanks,
Ben
Security Engineer | Aurora Inc
[Attachment: initial-sig-asks.pdf]

From: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@aurora-inc.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-11 10:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: least-privilege matrix + provisioning proof for SIG review

Ben —

Appreciate the clear asks. I'm looping in Karthik (identity) and Naomi (compliance) to assemble the artifacts. Plan:

1) I'll attach a concise access matrix (role -> permitted actions -> example policy snippets).
2) Karthik will export SAML/SCIM summary and attribute mapping (IdP metadata redacted where needed).
3) Naomi will provide a sanitized audit-log sample and confirm retention windows.

We should be able to get a packaged set to you within 24 hours. If Aurora wants to review live, I'm available Wed 9–11am PT.

Sofia Ivanova
Senior Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: none yet]

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@aurora-inc.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-11 13:42 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: least-privilege matrix + provisioning proof for SIG review

Ben / Sofia / Naomi —

Quick clarifications from the provisioning side to make sure we provide exactly what Aurora needs: 

- For SCIM, do you need a mapping of every attribute we sync, or just the attributes used to determine role assignment (e.g., department -> role)? We can export a full attribute spec or a condensed mapping.
- For SAML metadata, we will provide the SP metadata, ACS URL, and the recommended NameID format. We will redact customer-specific cert material.
- On RBAC: Redwood supports both role-based roles and scoped resource permissions. I'll include an example IAM policy JSON for the "support:read" and "project:admin" scopes.

I attached a draft access matrix (tabbed view), a 1-page SAML/SCIM config summary, and a sample audit CSV with user_provisioned events redacted to unique ids. Let me know if Aurora needs raw logs instead of CSV.

Attachments:
- sig_access_matrix_v2.xlsx (tab: matrix, tab: example_policies)
- saml_scim_config_summary.pdf
- audit-log-sample-2027Q1.csv

— Karthik
Lead Identity Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@aurora-inc.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aurora Procurement <procure@aurora-inc.com>
Date: 2027-04-12 08:20 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: least-privilege matrix + provisioning proof for SIG review

Team —

Thanks, that bundle looks great. A couple of quick follow-ups from our side after a brief review: 

- SCIM: we only need the condensed mapping that shows which attribute triggers role assignment (department, jobTitle, groups). The full attribute spec isn't necessary.
- RBAC question: can you confirm whether service accounts can be scoped to a single project and prevented from listing other projects? Our auditor flagged cross-project enumeration as a risk.
- Logs: the CSV sample is fine, but can you provide one example of the provisioning event that shows the timestamp, actor (system vs IdP), and the target user id (masked)?

We'd like to do a 20-min call at 10:00am PT today to sign off; will that work?

Ben
Security Engineer | Aurora Inc

From: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@aurora-inc.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-12 11:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: least-privilege matrix + provisioning proof for SIG review

Ben —

Thanks for the call today. Confirming the follow-ups we agreed on: 

- Attached: condensed SCIM->role mapping (tab 'condensed-mapping' in the workbook).
- RBAC: service accounts can be restricted to a single project; I included an example policy snippet in the matrix workbook that denies list/read on other projects unless explicitly granted.
- Audit example: the audit CSV includes a masked provisioning row showing timestamp (2027-03-29T14:02:17Z), actor=IdP, target_user_id=usr_8f3b****. We also provided the retention policy (90 days) in the SAML/SCIM summary.

Attachments in this message: sig_access_matrix_v2.xlsx (condensed-mapping tab), saml_scim_config_summary.pdf, audit-log-sample-2027Q1.csv

If Aurora is comfortable, we can upload these artifacts to the secure Drive link and share a short readout recording. Otherwise we'll push the DocuSign and procurement next steps once your security signoff is complete.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference
[Attachment stubs: sig_access_matrix_v2.xlsx, saml_scim_config_summary.pdf, audit-log-sample-2027Q1.csv]
